body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 9acdd7e8f6517aa95e988836e78c7a19ddea8134 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- Axis order, checked in `assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps` (`approach`, `departure`, `g30`):
  - Outside turning and threading (point outside the stock radius): `G0 X`, then `G0 Z`. The X move runs at G30's Z, and the Z move runs outside the diameter. Safe for any stored G30 outside the stock.
  - Boring and hole on centre (point inside the radius): `G0 Z` to the point, or to `ClearancePlane` when the point is on or behind the face, then `G0 X`, then `G0 Z` down. Without a `ClearancePlane` in front of the face, the post refuses by name.
  - Facing: the start is outside the radius, so it takes the X-then-Z order.
  - Closing `G30`, tool change and "home": the post writes `G0 X` out to the stock radius, then `G0 Z` out to the face. It uses `ClearancePlane` when the end point is on the corner. The lines go before the next section's notes and work offset word.
- Stock not stated: `stockEnv()` returns null and the post refuses by name ("no stock stated"). It does not guess. A section that ends inside the stock envelope, a feed or arc as the first motion after G30, and a missing Z are also refused by name. No motion is written after a refusal until a point is reached.
- PR #1681 is not needed. The post does not read `StockTurnRadius`. It uses the `StockXY*` box and `StockZTop`. No dependency on #1681.
- Goldens: 9 files changed (8 in `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/` and `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/tormach-lathe/tool_change.nc`). I read every hunk. Each hunk is one of two kinds: (a) a two-axis `G0` after G30 split into single-axis `G0` lines that end at the same point, or (b) a one-axis `G0 X` or `G0 Z` added before a `G30`. No other line changed. The turning goldens get no departure line because the last point is already outside the stock. All is explained by the change.
- Clean room: the sources are the public LinuxCNC G30 documentation. No vendor post text. Decision file `docs/decisions/1604-lathe-g30-rapid.md` is present. The PR does not touch `PROCESS_VERSION`, snapshots or `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Results (merged with main, locally; no runner or Actions run)**
- `camcraft-app` tests: `lathe_post_tormach_g30` 4 passed (new), `lathe_post_tormach`, `lathe_post_tormach_thread`, `lathe_cycle_exit`, `conformance`, `tormach_lathes`, `lathe_post_css`, `lathe_work_spindle`, `lathe_workholding_kinds`, `lathe_workholding_rpm`, `recorded_post_streams`: all ok, 0 failed.
- `camcraft-post` tests: `recorded_streams`, `script_tormach_lathe`, `explain_lathe`, `lathe_post_refusals`: all ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Mutation check: I swapped the outside approach to Z-then-X. Three of four pins failed (`the_first_move_after_g30_is_x_alone_then_z_alone`, `the_departure_goes_plus_x_then_plus_z_before_g30`, `no_stored_g30_outside_the_stock_is_reached_across_it`). I reverted the change.
- I did not run the whole quick gate. The author reports it green on this head.

**What no real control or simulator ran**
- No PathPilot or LinuxCNC control ran these programs. No machine simulator ran them. The "no G30 line crosses the stock" pin is a geometric check in the test over a grid of stored G30 positions. It checks the text of the program, not a real control. The PR body also lists the PathPilot lathe Hub run as not done. A hand test with G30 stored (a) on centre in front of the face and (b) beside the bar behind the face is still wanted.

**Requested before merge**
- None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. The stock radius is the largest half-width of the stock box. A square bar has a half-diagonal that is larger. A start point between the two would take the X-then-Z order across a bar corner. The PR names this as #1666 (P3). It is a wrong-order risk only for box stock on a lathe.
2. `departure()` accepts an end point exactly on the face (within `EPS`) as "in front of the face". The `+X` move then runs on the face plane. This does not cut, but a small margin or the `ClearancePlane` would be safer. #1681 may give a better radius later; the post then needs a follow-up to use it.
3. The PR body lists drafts #517, #518 and #468, which also change this post. The second one to merge refreshes from main.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
